column2: What is in the “⋯” menu and under the right-click?
column3: The same small action menu everywhere: Open, Edit, Rename, Duplicate, Export… and Delete in red at the very bottom. A right-click on a list row, a thumbnail or an object in an editor (Cut, Copy, Paste, Bring to front…, with their keys) opens this same menu, where the mouse is. Shift + right-click: the browser’s usual menu.

column2: How do I print a record, a booklet or a list?
column3: “🖨 Print” (or ⌘P) always opens the same window: the preview of the page, the size (A4, A5), Portrait or Landscape, what is printed (photos…), then “🖨 Print”. “⤓ PDF” makes a PDF file: in the print window, choose “Save as PDF”. Only the content of the screen is printed, without the menus.

column2: How do I print a presentation, a folded booklet, a slideshow or a single page?
column3: Everywhere, “🖨 Print” (or ⌘P in an editor, or “⤓ Export ▾ → 🖨 Print”) opens the same window, without a new tab. At the top: A4, A5 or ✎ Other, Portrait or Landscape. In the blue “What gets printed” area, the tool’s choices: slides with or without notes and how many per page, entries or table of the catalogue, one photo per page or a contact sheet, image and text of a transcription, bleed and crop marks of a page layout… Then “Pages”: All, The one shown, or Choose (“1-3, 7, 10-12”) and the number of copies. The preview on the right changes with each choice; ‹ › to see the other pages. The size and your choices are remembered for next time, tool by tool.

column2: How do I import my tree from Gramps?
column3: In Gramps: Family Trees → Export, choose “Gramps XML Package (family tree and media)”: you get a .gpkg file that contains the tree and its photos (a plain .gramps file works too, but without the photos). Then Settings → Import → “⤒ Import a tree…”: the window shows what will come in (people, families, places, sources, media, witnesses), then “⤒ Import”. Everything is taken over: multiple names (married name, nicknames), events with their witnesses, godfathers and godmothers, places with their hierarchy and coordinates, sources, citations and repositories, notes, labels (with their colour), attributes. Only the photos stored in the package are copied: a path that would point outside the package is refused. Right after, “↶ Undo” removes everything.

column2: How do I import a tree from Ancestry or MyHeritage?
column3: Export the tree as GEDCOM on the site (Ancestry: Trees → Tree Settings → Export Tree; MyHeritage: Family Tree → Export to GEDCOM), then Settings → Import → “⤒ Import a tree…”. The app recognises the site: married names, main photo, labels, links to the site’s records and documents (kept in the citations), dates written in English (“Abt. 1850”, “Bet. 1850 and 1855”). Photos that stayed on the site are never downloaded: their addresses are kept in an “🔗 Online media” note on the record. To add this tree to a database that is already filled without duplicates, use Settings → “Merge a tree” instead.

column2: How do I import my tree from RootsMagic, Family Tree Maker or Généatique?
column3: RootsMagic: Settings → Import → “⤒ Import a tree…” and choose your .rmtree (or .rmgc) file directly: it is read without being changed (people, names, families, adoptions, events, places and localities with coordinates, sources, citations, media, notes, witnesses). Family Tree Maker encrypts its .ftm files: no other software can open them; in FTM do “File → Export → GEDCOM”, then import the .ged (military service, adoptions _FREL / _MREL, main photo are understood). Généatique: its own file format is not documented; export a GEDCOM (File → Export): ANSI, ANSEL or UTF-8, places with locality and INSEE code, godfathers, godmothers and witnesses are taken over. For a cousin’s tree, “Merge a tree” also accepts the .rmtree.

column2: How do I import a GeneWeb file (.gw)?
column3: In GeneWeb, export the database as a .gw text file (the “gwu” command, or Geneanet’s .gw export). Then Settings → Import → “⤒ Import a tree…” and choose the .gw file: the window shows what will come in (people, families, events). Taken over: families and children, births, baptisms, deaths (also “killed”, “died young”), burials, events from the pevt and fevt blocks, witnesses, godparents, adoptions, notes, sources, titles, GeneWeb dates (about, before, after, between, Julian and Republican calendars). An unreadable block is skipped and reported. Right after, “↶ Undo” removes everything. A .gwb database (GeneWeb’s folder) cannot be read: you need the .gw.

column2: How do I import a GEDCOM-X file (FamilySearch)?
column3: Settings → Import → “⤒ Import a tree…” and choose the GEDCOM-X file, in JSON (.json) or XML (.xml). People, other names, couples, parent-child links (with adoption), dated and placed facts, places with coordinates, sources and pages, notes, FamilySearch and Wikidata identifiers are taken over. The GEDCOM-X exported by the app reads back without any notable loss.

column2: How do I import from Legacy, Family Historian, Ancestral Quest, Reunion, Ancestris, webtrees, Brother’s Keeper, PAF, WikiTree, Geni or GenoPro?
column3: Export a GEDCOM from that software or site, then Settings → Import → “⤒ Import a tree…”. The app recognises the software and keeps its special features: private records (_PRIV) → confidential, Legacy tags (_TAG) and Family Historian flags (_FLGS) → labels, webtrees “to do” → note, Wikidata identifier → record, adoptions (_FREL, _MREL), accents of old Mac or DOS files; other data specific to the software goes into a “Data specific to …” note. GenoPro’s .gno file is not read (no reliable public description): go through its GEDCOM export.

column2: How do I export my tree WITH the photos (GedZip, Gramps package)?
column3: Settings → Export → “⤓ To other software and sites” → “📦 GedZip with the photos” (GEDCOM 7 + media folder in a .gdz) or “🌳 Gramps package with the photos” (.gpkg). The window first gives the size and the number of files. With “For sharing”, living people and confidential records are hidden, and a photo showing one of these people is not put in the package. Both packages can be reopened here with “⤒ Import a tree”.

column2: What is a record’s Wikidata identifier for?
column3: For a well-known person (artist, mayor, scientist…), the Wikidata “Q…” number is noted in the “External references” block (✎). It gives a ↗ link to their page, and the “🌐 Complete from Wikidata” button: only when you click, the app reads the Wikidata entry on the Internet and shows you what is missing in your database (birth, death with the place, sex, occupation, a note with the description and the Wikipedia links). Nothing is replaced; you tick what you keep, and “↶ Undo” removes everything right after. The identifier also goes into GEDCOM and GEDCOM-X exports.

column2: How do I put my tree on Geneanet?
column3: Settings → Export → “⤓ To other software and sites” → “🌐 For Geneanet”: a GEDCOM ready for Geneanet (UTF-8, places in the format “[Locality] - Commune, INSEE code, department, region, country”). Living people and confidential records are always hidden: anonymous (“Living person”, to keep the links between branches) or removed, as you choose. Geneanet does not receive the photos: only those with an online address go, as a link. Then on Geneanet: My tree → Import a GEDCOM file.

column2: How do I move my tree into Gramps, or send it as GEDCOM-X (FamilySearch)?
column3: Settings → Export → “⤓ To other software and sites”: “🌳 To Gramps” makes a .gramps file (in Gramps: Family Trees → Import) with places arranged by country, region, department, commune; “🔗 GEDCOM-X” makes FamilySearch’s JSON. Tick “For sharing” to hide living people and confidential records. The photos are not in these files, only their names.

column2: How do I put the family’s birthdays and name days in my calendar?
column3: Settings → Export → “📅 Birthday calendar” (or Family calendar → ⤓ Export the birthdays): choose your ancestors (Sosa), the whole database or a branch, only the living or everyone, and births, marriages, deaths and 🎉 name days. The .ics file opens in Apple, Google or Outlook; each date comes back every year (a 29 February: the last day of February). Approximate dates (about, before…) are left aside and counted. Confidential records are never in it.

column2: How do I put my cousins and the archive services in my phone’s contacts?
column3: Settings → Export → “📇 Contacts” (or Lists → Directory of the living → ⤓ Export ▾): a vCard file (.vcf) with the addresses, e-mails and phone numbers you noted: directory of the living, archive services, DNA cousins, correspondents in the letter register. Open it on your phone or your computer.

column2: How do I see my family’s places in Google Earth?
column3: Settings → Export → “🗺 Places (KML)” (or Lists → Places → ⤓ Export ▾): a .kml file with one folder per kind of event (Birth, Marriage, Death…) and one marker per place. “🗺 Places (GeoJSON)” does the same for QGIS, uMap… Places without coordinates are left aside; the events of hidden living people are not included.

column2: How do I import my genealogy society’s transcriptions (Nimègue)?
column3: Settings → Import → “📜 A society’s transcriptions (Nimègue…)”, or Lists → Record indexes → “⤒ Import transcriptions”. A Nimègue file (v2 or v3, with or without a header line, even in an old Windows encoding) or a society’s CSV, Excel or LibreOffice table: the columns are recognised automatically (date, surname, first name, father, mother, godfather, witnesses, shelfmark, image…) and you can correct them in the preview. Each record becomes a line in the record index of its commune, with its people and their role (child, spouse, deceased, father, godmother…). Tick “Create or link the records”: for each person who looks like a record in your database, the app asks “is this the same person?” — nothing is linked or created without your choice, a person mentioned in several records gives only one record, and an existing record is never changed. A record already imported is pointed out. Right after, “↶ Undo” removes everything.

column2: How do I import my family from an Excel or LibreOffice spreadsheet?
column3: Settings → Import → “👥 Table of people”. One row per person: first name, surname, sex, dates (written as in a record: “7 May 1925”, “about 1784”, “08/12/1960”), places, occupation, note, and the father, mother and spouse links by row number, by name (“Pierre MARTIN”) or by Sosa number (2 and 3 are the parents of 1…). The preview shows the records, couples and children that will come in, and the links that could not be made (a name used by two rows, unknown number). If a person may already be in your database, you choose: the same record, or create one. “↶ Undo” removes everything right after. Cells that contain a spreadsheet formula are never taken over.

column2: How do I exchange my sources with Zotero, EndNote or JabRef (RIS, BibTeX)?
column3: To bring references in: Settings → Import → “📚 References (RIS, BibTeX)” — each one becomes a source in your database, ready to cite (title, authors, publisher or archive service, date, address, shelfmark, notes; accents understood, even written the LaTeX way). A source already there is not taken again. To send them out: Settings → Export → “⤓ Sources (RIS, BibTeX)”. The exported file reads back without loss. The Research workshop has its own .bib and .ris buttons, which also keep the archive collection, the shelfmark and the notes.
